schemes.definition: A company or organization that develops, publishes, sells, or maintains software, hardware, or related technology products.
A flaw, weakness, or bug in software, hardware, or a system that can be exploited to compromise security.
An application, utility, plugin, or system software package designed for end users or computing environments.
System software that manages computer hardware and software resources and provides common services for computer programs.
A distinct sovereign state, nation, or territorial body with its own government and defined geographical borders.
An official department, ministry, service, or administrative organization operating as part of a state or sovereign government.
A formal public notice or bulletin issued by an organization detailing security vulnerabilities, remediation steps, or software updates.
An individual human being, such as a government official, cybersecurity expert, researcher, or executive.
A computer file, document, script, or archive used as an attack vector, payload carrier, or indicator of compromise.
A commercial company or organization that provides information security products, threat intelligence, incident response, or security research services.
A numerical label assigned to a device connected to a computer network utilizing the Internet Protocol for communication.
An identification string or namespace defining a realm of administrative autonomy or authority within the Domain Name System.
A unique identifier representing an electronic mail destination used to send and receive digital messages across networks.
An intergovernmental or transnational institution established by treaty or agreement among sovereign states.
An individual or organized group responsible for conducting malicious cyber activities, attacks, or cyberespionage campaigns.
An online platform or service that facilitates social networking, user interaction, and content sharing.
An armed force, military unit, command, or defense institution operating as part of a state's armed services.
An internet-hosted platform, application, or utility providing specific online functionality, content, or API services to users.
A non-profit, citizen-based group or civil society organization operating independently of any government.
An institute, think tank, or specialized unit dedicated to conducting scientific, policy, strategic, or security research.
A collection of connected Internet Protocol routing prefixes under the control of network operators presenting a single, clearly defined routing policy.
A company or organization that provides voice, data, mobile, or internet communication services to subscribers.
A large human settlement, municipality, or designated urban administrative area.
An organization or specialized team responsible for monitoring, analyzing, and responding to cybersecurity incidents and threats.
